newsitem.title: USA: Rowland likely to veto Conn. budget - report.
newsitem.headline: Rowland likely to veto Conn. budget - report.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland (R) is likely to veto a state budget hammered out at the last minute by frustrated Democrats, the Hartford Courant reported Tuesday.
The Democrats earlier Tuesday morning approved a two-year, $21.1 billion budget, which called for both higher spending and lower tax cuts than Rowland had proposed.
Democrats, who control both chambers of the legislature, proposed a combined $360 million in tax cuts compared with the governor's $445 million.
This year's legislative session ends at midnight Wednesday.
State Republicans blasted the budget proposal, saying it was filled with holes and had too much spending and too few tax breaks.
The Democrats' spending plan is still $635 million above Rowland's plan, which would have increased spending by about 1 percent over two years.
